verdict.rationale: Auth0's docs show it acting as an OAuth 2.0 authorization server for your own API. It issues access tokens to registered clients via the client credentials and device flows, and it handles scopes and permissions for "third-party integrations" as well as first-party apps. The evidence does not show the full "Sign in with my app" provider experience for outside developers. Missing for 10: documented third-party application registration (static or dynamic client registration), a user consent screen for third-party clients, OIDC identity tokens for external relying parties, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
